uncited: It builds on [Data Feature-Based Classification](5934-data-feature-based-classification.md) by extending the input domain from scalar values to multi-dimensional feature vectors derived from color and geometry.
The classification function takes a feature vector $\mathbf{x}$ constructed from the voxel's color, its six immediate neighbors' colors, and its position.
**Neighbor Colors:** 6 neighbors $\times$ 3 dimensions ($R, G, B$) = 18 dimensions.
The neighbors are defined as the six immediate spatial neighbors (likely $\pm x, \pm y, \pm z$ in the grid).
**Training Data Acquisition:** The user paints on 2D slices passing through the volume to provide training data.
**Classification:** Evaluate the high-dimensional classification function $C(\mathbf{x})$ to determine the opacity $\alpha$.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** Voxels on the volume boundary have fewer than 6 neighbors.
*   **Limitations:** The high-dimensional feature space (up to 24 dimensions) may require careful tuning of the classification function.
